Comment: DataMartMigrationStateMachine — retry-safe, chunked, resumable schema-migration of the four per-document rollup tables to the widened (document_class) grain. Orchestrated as a Step Functions state machine so per-chunk retries have their own Lambda budget instead of sharing one 15-min invocation. Replaces the earlier Lambda-only backfill_migrate design that thrashed on real-volume stacks. See docs/reporting-sql-layer.md §Track A and the CHANGELOG entry for the design rationale.

CheckMarker.Comment: Read the SSM migration marker and return a routing decision (short_circuit | skip_purge | full_flow). Compares marker against BOTH days AND version — a future MigrationVersion bump for a new schema change must NOT short-circuit against a completed marker from the prior version. See _check_marker_state in the rollup Lambda for the backward-compat rule that treats a marker with no version= segment as matching (one-time transition).

RouteOnMarkerState.Comment: Route based on the marker check. Completed → done (no work). In-progress from prior run → skip purge, only re-run backfill. Otherwise → full flow starting with purge.

MigrationAlreadyDone.Comment: Marker says state=completed for the current days value. Migration was already run cleanly on a previous invocation; nothing to do.

InitialPurge.Comment: Delete every S3 object under the four per-document rollup prefixes so we can repopulate at the widened (document_class) grain without colliding with pre-widening parquet. Idempotent — a re-run on an already-empty prefix is fast.

WriteInProgressMarker.Comment: Write the SSM marker as state=in_progress IMMEDIATELY after purge, BEFORE any backfill chunk runs. This is load-bearing: any state-machine restart (via CustomResource re-fire, operator intervention, etc.) will read this marker and SKIP the purge — chunks already written survive. Includes 'version' so CheckMarker on a future run can compare it against the request's MigrationVersion.

PlanChunks.Comment: Compute the list of (start, end) time ranges to iterate. The CFN CustomResource passes ChunkHours=1 (see template.yaml::DataMartMigrationCustomResource), which is the ACTUAL default in production — 720 one-hour chunks over the 30 d window. plan_migration_chunks's Lambda-side default of 24 h only applies to a caller that omits the ChunkHours field entirely (never happens through the dispatcher). 1 h chunks are used deliberately so per-chunk retries have the tightest possible blast radius.

MigrateChunks.Comment: Iterate each 1 h chunk, invoking mode: backfill per chunk. MaxConcurrency=8 in 2.1.6 (was 1) — pairs with the rollup Lambda's ReservedConcurrentExecutions=12 to run 8 chunks in parallel × 2 Athena INSERTs each = 16 concurrent DML queries, leaving 4 slots under Athena's default 20-per-workgroup DML concurrency for the scheduled crons that share this Lambda. Cuts a 720-hour migration from ~2 h serial → ~20 min. Idempotency guards (HeadObject-skip per partition + Athena ClientRequestToken dedup) make the parallel writes safe. SFN-native Retry replaces the async Lambda retries the earlier design relied on.

BackfillChunk.Comment: 2.1.5: arms restricted to metering_hourly + metering_docs_hourly. Those are the ONLY two rollup tables the widening deploy changed the schema of; control_plane_hourly and data_plane_lambda_hourly (a) don't have document_class, (b) were never purged, (c) are already populated by the routine :05 hourly cron. Including them here was scope creep that (a) doubles per-chunk time and (b) surfaced empty-CW-hour 'no rows' partial failures that blocked WriteCompletedMarker on qs1 execution cc6b01b3.

BackfillDailyRange.Comment: Iterate each day in the retention window and invoke the daily-rollup INSERTs. Runs AFTER MigrateChunks so metering_hourly / metering_docs_hourly are fully populated (the daily rollups aggregate from those). Single Lambda invocation because per-day daily rollup work is small (~5-10 s per day × 30 days ≈ 150-300 s, fits in Lambda's 900 s budget). Without this task, metering_daily and metering_docs_daily stay empty for 30 days waiting for the scheduled 00:15 UTC daily rollup to catch up one day at a time.

CheckMigrationSuccess.Comment: Aggregate the Map state's per-chunk results PLUS the daily-backfill result. Returns all_hours_clean=true only when EVERY chunk AND the daily backfill reported hours_failed=0 AND hours_partial=0 — both counters must be zero. In the migration context a partial-hour result (some rollup arms succeeded, others didn't for the same hour) IS a blocker because a customer table with rows silently missing is not an acceptable end state; the 2026-09-22 incident on qs1 where 38 chunks reported partial and zero rows landed in metering_hourly is why _check_hours_failed treats partial as unclean. Routine hourly-cron ops treat partial as tolerated (reconciler will fill later), but MIGRATION does not. Passes chunk_results and daily_result as separate fields because ASL has no ArrayConcat intrinsic; the aggregator in the Lambda handles the union.

MigrationOutcome.Comment: If every chunk was clean, mark migration completed; otherwise fail explicitly (marker stays in_progress so operator can restart the state machine and it resumes from where it left off, skipping the purge).

WriteCompletedMarker.Comment: Migration succeeded end-to-end: write the SSM marker as state=completed so future state-machine invocations short-circuit at CheckMarker. This is the ONLY completion signal customers should watch — CFN UPDATE_COMPLETE fires immediately after the CustomResource dispatcher returns and is decoupled from actual migration completion. Includes 'version' so a future migration for a different schema change routes to full flow instead of short-circuiting against this one.

MigrationHadFailures.Comment: At least one chunk reported hours_failed > 0. The marker stays state=in_progress so restarting the state machine (via CustomResource re-fire or manual StartExecution) will resume from the failed chunks — the Purge is skipped, already-written chunks are HeadObject-skipped, only the failing hours are retried. Alarm on this failure via SFN's built-in CloudWatch integration.
MigrationHadFailures.Cause: One or more chunks reported hours_failed > 0. Marker left as state=in_progress. Restart the state machine (or wait for the next CustomResource fire) to resume.
